raw_response.rationale: The paper reports inferential statistics (Welch's one-way ANOVAs on N = 97 survey respondents, plus OLS regressions, bivariate correlations, and a bootstrap mediation model on N = 90), alongside purely descriptive restroom use-time observations (24 men, 32 women). However, none of the inferential models empirically test a rule-type legal, regulatory, building-code, tariff, ownership, or administrative exposure (narrow Criterion 2). Instead, all tested predictors are individual respondent demographics (gender, age group) or a composite of self-reported adverse restroom experiences predicting attitudinal ratings and perceived safety/satisfaction. While the article doctrinally compares international building-code approaches and proposes a tripartite regulatory accountability matrix, no legal or institutional rule varies empirically in the quantitative analyses, making it out of scope for SWiM synthesis.
